questionContract.instructions: Using only state.repository as evidence and applying state.rules, which statement describes this repository's plugins and configuration?

criteria.supported: This repository documents an installable agent plugin or non-skill agent configuration: MCP client launch settings, hooks, slash commands, subagent definitions, harness rules/configuration or interface extensions. Built-in agent profiles and agent-specific launch, prompt or model settings also qualify. A plugin installation/invocation command pointing to this repository or a local plugin directory (for example, claude --plugin-dir ./...) establishes an owned plugin, including one that bundles skills. MCP client configuration supplied inline in this README is a configuration deliverable, even when the configured server belongs to another repository.
criteria.not_supported: No plugin or non-skill agent configuration is documented. SKILL.md packages, their top-level skill router, and copying skill folders into a skills directory are skill delivery alone. External plugin links or general plugin usage instructions do not establish an owned plugin. Generic product/server/trainer settings alone are not agent configuration.

evidence.text: MarkItDown is a lightweight Python utility for converting various files to Markdown for use with LLMs and related text analysis pipelines. To this end, it is most comparable to [textract](https://github.com/deanmalmgren/textract), but with a focus on preserving important document structure and content as Markdown (including: headings, lists, tables, links, etc.) While the output is often reasonably presentable and human-friendly, it is meant to be consumed by text analysis tools -- and may not be the best option for high-fidelity document conversions for human consumption.
MarkItDown also supports 3rd-party plugins. Plugins are disabled by default. To list installed plugins:
To find available plugins, search GitHub for the hashtag `#markitdown-plugin`. To develop a plugin, see `packages/markitdown-sample-plugin`.

The `markitdown-ocr` plugin adds OCR support to PDF, DOCX, PPTX, and XLSX converters, extracting text from embedded images using LLM Vision — the same `llm_client` / `llm_model` pattern that MarkItDown already uses for image descriptions. No new ML libraries or binary dependencies required.
Pass the same `llm_client` and `llm_model` you would use for image descriptions:
To use Large Language Models for image descriptions (currently only for pptx and image files), provide `llm_client` and `llm_model`:
md = MarkItDown(llm_client=client, llm_model="gpt-4o", llm_prompt="optional custom prompt")

MarkItDown is a Python utility for converting files to Markdown for use with LLMs and related text analysis pipelines. This repository is intended to provide Python libraries that can be incorporated into other systems — not the end-user applications built on top of them.
### Extending MarkItDown Without Changing This Repository
MarkItDown supports 3rd-party plugins, so support for a new format can be published and installed independently of this repository:
See `packages/markitdown-sample-plugin` to get started, and tag your repository `#markitdown-plugin` so that others can find it.

changes.reason: The README owns general document-conversion/OCR plugins. Their documented behavior extends file converters and uses an LLM client for image descriptions; it does not document an installable agent/harness plugin, agent configuration or an agent-interface extension. The owned markitdown-mcp package is a program/agent integration; the sent README provides no MCP client launch settings or other non-skill agent configuration. General LLM-related conversion plugins and the existence of an MCP server do not separately establish form.extensions under the frozen definition. No requirement for a standalone product, extra implementation file or owned backend is imposed.
changes.retainedOtherLabels: This finding does not negate form.tools, capability.interaction, office or research. It does not exclude an actual agent plugin merely because it also performs conversion/OCR.
